Small deterministic color fixtures. They contain no user image pixels.

- `libraw-prophoto-d65-linear.icc`: the exact 496-byte matrix/linear profile
  generated by LibRaw 0.22.2 for output color space 4. Its white is D65; do not
  replace it with a standard ProPhoto D50 profile.
- `synthetic-gray.icc`: LittleCMS-generated D50 gray profile, gamma 2.2.
- `synthetic-cmyk.icc`: generated synthetic four-channel input LUT. It is a test
  function, not a Fogra/US/European printing characterization.
- `synthetic-rgb-lut.icc`: generated RGB-to-Lab input LUT, exercising the
  non-matrix profile route to XYZ float32.
- `synthetic-matrix-and-lut.icc`: the matrix/TRC fixture with an additional
  RGB-to-XYZ A2B0 LUT. `cmsIsMatrixShaper` is true, but the native conversion
  selects the LUT. `mixed-icc-fixture.c` regenerates this deliberate priority
  case; its LUT does not characterize an actual camera or display.

`color-oracle.c` creates the gray/CMYK fixtures and independently converts native
uint16 samples using the system LittleCMS. Compile it against LittleCMS 2.19.1.
The tests compare RGB16 and RGB8 output hashes against this native reference,
using 4,096 deterministic input pixels per case. All 73,728 output components
were identical in the initial native ARM/WASM qualification. The output-profile
creation timestamp is not part of the pixel hash.

The oracle accepts output bit argument 32 for XYZ float32 (PCS D50). Matrix and
RGB LUT cases each compare 12,288 float32 components to native LittleCMS;
all components matched exactly in the initial qualification. A separate test
modifies a matrix colorant to a negative coordinate and verifies that the float
transport adds no gamut clamp. Profile tags rXYZ/gXYZ/bXYZ/wtpt/chad are exposed
as stored, without assuming that a missing chad implies a particular adaptation.
